name: Video Library
description: Videos from LBRY and Odysee: browse, search, follow channels and watch
summary: Built for this screen: Odysee's front page one big card to a row, videos that play in the page with controls made for a finger, and fullscreen turned on its side.

name: Couch for Trakt
description: A movie and TV tracker for Trakt: discover, up next, calendar, watchlist and history
summary: Built for this screen: posters two across, a page per film or show, and the calendar as one scrolling list, with tabs at the bottom.

name: Airwaves
description: Internet radio from radio-browser.info: 50,000 stations by genre, country and language
summary: Built for this screen: genres and stations in rows a thumb can scroll, a station list per genre, and tabs at the bottom.

name: Crypto Market
description: CoinGecko prices, coin pages, a watchlist and a portfolio
summary: Built for this screen: the market as one list, a coin page with its chart and stats, and a watchlist, with tabs at the bottom.

name: Vitals
description: A task manager for a Linux phone: processor, memory, tasks and network
summary: Built for this screen: processor, memory, tasks and network as cards with live graphs, one tab each.

name: Transit
description: Public transport journeys and live departures, worldwide, on Transitous
summary: Built for this screen: a journey planner and live departure boards with tabs at the bottom, big touch targets and nothing cut off.

name: Tic-tac-toe
description: Noughts and crosses against the phone, or across a table
summary: Built for this screen: the score over the board and the two buttons under it, a record of each difficulty a tap away, and square marks in the theme's own colours.

name: Minesweeper
description: Clear the field without opening a mine
summary: Built for this screen: a portrait board of thumb-sized cells, a flag button that latches, a clock that stops with the window, and a record per level.

name: Reversi
description: Play Reversi against the phone, or across a table
summary: Built for this screen: the board edge to edge with the score over it, an opponent that thinks on its own thread, and Undo and New game under your thumb.

name: Chess
description: Play chess against the phone, or across a table
summary: Built for this screen: two taps a move on a full-width board, three levels to play against, promotion as a sheet, and the game kept when you leave.

name: Mill
description: Nine Men's Morris against the phone, or across a table
summary: Built for this screen: the three squares full width, pieces in hand counted over them, and the rule everybody forgets shown when it applies.

name: Solitaire
description: Klondike patience, one tap a move
summary: Built for this screen: seven columns sized to fit 360 px, one tap a move, and Send them home when every card is face up.

name: Peg Solitaire
description: Jump pegs until one is left, on nine solvable figures
summary: Built for this screen: a board of big pegs, nine figures that can all be solved, and a hint that shows the next jump of a real solution.

name: Five Letters
description: Guess the five-letter word in six tries
summary: Built for this screen: the grid and its own keyboard on one page, a mark as well as a colour on every tile, and a record of each day's guesses.

name: Breakout
description: Knock the wall down without losing the ball
summary: Built for this screen: a full-height field, a bat that follows your thumb, five walls, and a clock that stops when the window closes.

name: Notes
description: Text notes and checklists, kept on the device
summary: Built for this screen: notes and checklists as lined cards two across, one tap to open and write, pinned ones first, and search at the top.

name: Habits
description: Track habits with a tap a day, kept on the device
summary: Built for this screen: a row per habit with the last days to tap, a page per habit with its streak and sixteen weeks of history, and achievements.

name: Launches
description: Upcoming rocket launches, and the ones you star
summary: Built for this screen: the next launches with live countdowns, a page per launch with its pad, window and orbit, and the ones you star on a tab of their own.

name: Food
description: Point the camera at a barcode for nutrition facts
summary: Built for this screen: the camera as the first page, a product page with Nutri-Score, nutrition per 100 g and allergens, and everything you scanned kept.

name: Calculator
description: The four operations, a tape you can tap, and arithmetic in tens
summary: Built for this screen: big square keys with the sum above them, arithmetic that counts in tens so 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3, and a tape of past sums.

name: Weather
description: Now, the next day and the week, where you are and in the places you named
summary: Built for this screen: now, the next hours and the week in one scrolling column, and the places you named a tap away.

name: Clock
description: The time, an alarm that says when it is late, a stopwatch and a timer
summary: Built for this screen: alarms, a stopwatch with laps and a timer, one tab each, with a dial big enough to read across a room.

name: Calendar
description: The month, the day under it, and what is next
summary: Built for this screen: the month with the chosen day's events under it, an agenda of what is next, and events kept in one file with no accounts.

name: Contacts
description: A name, a number, an email, and a note — one file, no accounts
summary: Built for this screen: one searchable list by letter, a page per person to edit, and everything kept in one file on the phone.

name: Files
description: One folder at a time
summary: Built for this screen: one folder at a time with a crumb trail above it, places a tab away, and copy, move, rename and trash from a sheet.

name: Text Editor
description: One text file at a time, and an $EDITOR that waits
summary: Built for this screen: recent files a tap away, one file on the whole screen in a monospace face, and nothing lost when a file is closed unsaved.

name: Mail
description: Read and write email
summary: Built for this screen: one account over IMAP and SMTP, the inbox as one list, a message on a page of its own with no HTML drawn, and folders a tap away.
